Tlingit

A Tlingit starting path benefits from both institutional and community-specific histories. The Central Council’s own timeline records political advocacy, while a 2015 collaborative study examines Yakutat Tlingit relationships with the southern Wrangell–St.Elias region. The Yakutat case is one regional history within a wider people.

Read the sources [1] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska [2] National Park Service / Portland State University, with Yakutat Tlingit participants

Landscape context specifically for the Yakutat regional case, not all Tlingit homelands or a community portrait. The study places Hubbard Glacier within its Yakutat study region and records Yakutat Tlingit concerns about cruise traffic at Hubbard/Disenchantment Bay. No exclusive territory or independently verified wildlife claim inferred. This is landscape context for the Yakutat regional study. Its introduction and selected interview discussion identify Hubbard Glacier and adjacent waters as a Yakutat Tlingit concern. It is not all Tlingit homelands, a community portrait, a boundary or evidence of current glacier extent, climate trends or seal distributions. Complete available retrieved JPEG imported unchanged. 01

Identity and context

Tlingit people have homelands along the northwest coast and into adjoining inland regions.

Read the sources [1] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Lingít language, clans and houses, territorial histories and distinct contemporary governments. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska [2] National Park Service / Portland State University, with Yakutat Tlingit participants [3] tlingitandhaida.gov

03

Reading a tribal government’s own history

The Central Council’s timeline connects its institutional development with Alaska Native Brotherhood advocacy and efforts to seek redress for land withdrawals. It begins by recognizing Tlingit and Haida as distinct peoples. Read this as the government’s own historical account, alongside local histories; the statutes and cases it names require separate inspection.

Read the sources [1] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska

04

A Yakutat case with a stated method

Deur and colleagues’2015 study combines written records with interviews and guidance from Yakutat Tlingit representatives. Its opening pages challenge the idea that park landscapes are empty of human history and explain the report’s regional focus and limits. Yakutat relationships with coastal and glacial places should not be generalized to every Tlingit community.

Read the sources [2] National Park Service / Portland State University, with Yakutat Tlingit participants

History - Tlingit & Haida ↗

Read the Central Council’s timeline of political advocacy and institutional development. The government’s own narrative explicitly begins with Tlingit and Haida as distinct peoples; it is not a history of every Tlingit government.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete Our History timeline and Generations to Come/mission body, web lines 65–119; leadership biographies and linked laws/cases not separately reviewed.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public actual HTML body read. This is the Central Council’s institutional history and interpretation, not every Tlingit or Haida community’s government. Underlying statutes, court records, amounts and present rights not independently checked; no demographic totals or ceremonies reproduced.

https://tlingitandhaida.gov/about-us/history/

Yakutat Tlingit Ethnographic Study ↗

Publication: 2015

Selected introduction and methods explain collaboration with Yakutat Tlingit representatives, written-source emphasis and interview limits. A selected later paragraph records attributed concern about Hubbard Glacier cruise traffic; no sensitive sites or ecological finding adopted.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: 2015 report: printed pp. 1–6 and8–9/PDF pp. 9–14 and16–17, plus printed p. 173/PDF p. 181. Title/authors read;350-page report not read in full.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal public PDF 200 downloaded; actual selected page text read with pypdf. Academic/NPS synthesis with Yakutat Tlingit participation; underlying interviews/archives, all chapters, maps, figures and current legal/ecological conditions not independently reviewed. Specific clan narratives and sensitive-place details excluded.

https://www.nps.gov/wrst/learn/historyculture/upload/YakutatTlingit-EOA.pdf
